title: ✈️ Arrival in Tokyo
morning: Leave Narberth PA at 6:30 AM to arrive at SNAP Parking by 8:30 AM (1 hr 47 min drive, 99.3 miles). Drop off car at valet, then 10-minute ride to Newark (EWR Terminal C). Check bags and board UA131 in Premium Economy. Hydrate early and stay on destination time as much as possible.
daytime: In transit across the Pacific, prioritize rest blocks, water, and light movement every few hours so arrival day is manageable.
night: Land at Haneda, clear immigration/customs, withdraw startup cash, and take Limousine Bus to Keio Plaza.
details: 🅿️ Parking: SNAP Parking (Covered Valet) — Rental ID 123520709. Cost $281.20 (paid via SpotHero).
🚗 Drive from Narberth PA to SNAP Parking: 1 hr 47 min (99.3 miles). SNAP valet transfer to EWR Terminal C: ~10 min.
✈️ Flight: UA131 (EWR → HND), approx. 14 hours.
🛂 Arrival flow: Visit Japan Web QR → ATM → bus ticket counter.

🚌 Limousine Bus (HND → Keio Plaza): Buy ticket at the Arrivals Lobby counter (look for 'Airport Limousine' signs). Cost ~¥1,300. Journey ~75 min to Keio Plaza Hotel Shinjuku stop. Buses run every 20–30 min. No reservation needed — pay at counter.
🏨 Hotel: Keio Plaza Hotel (Shinjuku).
🎯 Goal: survive travel day and minimize decision fatigue.
note: Long-haul transition day. Keep expectations low and recover quickly.

brief.ops: UA131, eSIM, cash, bus to Keio Plaza

timeline.activity: Leave Narberth PA for SNAP Parking.
Arrive at SNAP Parking (Covered Valet). Travel time: 1 hr 47 min (99.3 miles).
Drop off car at SNAP Parking — Rental ID 123520709. Reserved through May 24 - June 4.
Check in, check bags, and proceed through security at EWR Terminal C.
Flight UA 131 Departs EWR (Terminal C). Seat: Premium Economy. Duration: ~14 Hours.
Arrive Haneda Terminal 3. Clear immigration/customs, activate eSIM if needed, withdraw startup cash, and confirm IC card/mobile Suica readiness.
Buy Airport Limousine Bus ticket at the arrivals lobby counter/kiosk for Keio Plaza Hotel Shinjuku. If the next direct hotel bus is delayed, use the next Shinjuku-area bus or taxi as backup.
Arrive Keio Plaza Hotel Shinjuku and check in. Keep bags/simple reset first; do not add sightseeing if energy is low.

title: 🛍️ Shibuya & Harajuku
splitNote: Dave/Debbie may split for different interests
morning: Start in Shinjuku, then take the Yamanote Line to Harajuku for Meiji Jingu Shrine before crowds. Keep the pace easy while body clocks adjust.
daytime: Work through Harajuku and Shibuya: Takeshita Street, @Cosme, optional SHARE LOUNGE rest stop at Shibuya Sakura Stage, then Shibuya Sky and crossing viewpoints.
night: Use the booked 2:00 PM Shibuya Sky entry as the afternoon anchor, then do Shibuya Crossing photos and shopping before heading to Shinjuku for the capybara café.
details: 📍 Primary anchors: Meiji Jingu Shrine → Harajuku → Shibuya Crossing → Shibuya Sky.
☔ Rain backup: Nakano Broadway (indoor-heavy).
🥞 Food target: crepes + snacks throughout, with a real lunch/rest buffer before Shibuya Sky.

🛋️ Optional 12:45 PM rest stop: SHARE LOUNGE at TSUTAYA Shibuya Sakura Stage (4F). Time-based lounge with soft drinks/snacks, walk-in OK, ~¥1,870/hr adult soft-drink plan; app payment may save 10%. It is a rest stop near Shibuya Station, not a Shibuya Crossing viewpoint.
👟 Keep feet fresh: this is a high-step urban day.
✂️ First cut if tired: shorten Harajuku/Cat Street shopping so the 2:00 PM Shibuya Sky and 5:15 PM CAPPINESS Shinjuku anchors stay easy.
note: Acclimation + iconic Tokyo visuals in one compact zone.

brief.today: Harajuku + SHARE LOUNGE + Shibuya Sky + CAPPINESS Shinjuku
brief.ops: Yamanote Line; SHARE LOUNGE Sakura Stage; Shibuya Sky QSJ919058; CAPPINESS Shinjuku 5JFRH9B 5:15 PM

goal: Acclimatize. Soak in the neon. Shibuya Crossing.

timeline.activity: Meiji Jingu Shrine (Yoyogi Park). Subway: Yamanote Line (Shinjuku -> Harajuku).
Harajuku (Takeshita Street + Cat Street). Browse the shops and snack stands, then pick a real lunch or coffee rest before walking toward Shibuya. If jet lag hits, skip deeper Cat Street shopping.

Optional rest stop: SHARE LOUNGE at TSUTAYA Shibuya Sakura Stage (4F, near Shibuya Station south side). Time-based lounge with soft drinks/snacks included; walk-in OK, ~¥1,870/hr per adult soft-drink plan, app payment may save 10%. Good air-conditioned break before Shibuya Sky. Note: this is not a Shibuya Crossing viewpoint.
Shibuya Sky (Booked). Ticket: 3 x Adult (Aged 12+), booking QSJ919058. Sunset/golden-hour slots were sold out, so this is an early-afternoon view.
Shibuya Crossing and shopping at Tokyu Hands or Loft. Photo Op: Mag's Park (Rooftop of Magnet building) or Starbucks.
🦙 CAPPINESS Shinjuku — capybara café (Booking ID: 5JFRH9B). Yamanote Line from Shibuya ~10 min. See bookings page for full details.

rainyDayOption: Go straight to **Nakano Broadway** (Indoor Otaku Mall) instead of Harajuku. See: [Rainy Day Options](../Reference/rainy-day-options.md)
keyPhrases: "Shashin o totte moraemasu ka?" (Could you take a photo for us?)
"Eigo no menyu wa arimasu ka?" (Do you have an English menu?)

title: 🐟 Toyosu, Ginza & Roppongi
morning: Relaxed start; head to Toyosu Market for a late-morning visit before heading to Ginza.
daytime: Structured Ginza shopping block: Itoya Ginza, Uniqlo Ginza, Onitsuka Tiger.
night: Roppongi art stop at Mori Art Museum (open late).
details: ☔ Rain resilience: Toyosu + Ginza + Mori Art Museum are all indoors.
🕙 Mori Art Museum stays open until 10 PM — no rush on timing.
note: Balanced day: food market, Ginza shopping, and a flexible evening art stop.

brief.ops: Tsukiji Line to Shijo-mae for Toyosu

goal: Fresh fish, Ginza luxury, and an evening art hit in Roppongi.

timeline.activity: Toyosu Market (Outer Market). Walk the outer market stalls for fresh sashimi-grade seafood. Tuna auction requires advance lottery (skip unless pre-booked). Eat: Sushidai or Daiwa Sushi (arrive early to avoid 2-hour waits).
Ginza — walk the main boulevard. See: Ginza Six (flagship mall), Itoya Ginza (stationery store), Hermès building (Renzo Piano glass tower). Eat: Lunch at any basement food hall (depachika).
Roppongi Hills. See: Mori Art Museum (top floor, city views), Louise Bourgeois spider sculpture in the courtyard. Skip: Mori Tower observation deck (overpriced, city guide alternatives are better).

keyPhrases: "Omakase de onegaishimasu." (I'll leave it to you / Chef's choice.)
"Kore wa nan desu ka?" (What is this?)

title: ⛩️ Asakusa & Akihabara
morning: Start with an Old Tokyo block: choose Yanaka first if you want quiet lanes, or go straight to Senso-ji and Kappabashi Kitchen Town if shopping energy is higher.
daytime: Head to Akihabara: Super Potato, Mandarake Complex, arcades, and nearby electronics browsing.
night: Flexible close: optional themed cafe or Kanda Myojin.
details: 🛍️ Tax-free opportunity day for shopping-heavy stops.
☔ Akihabara is rain-friendly due to indoor concentration.
📝 Carry a short target list to avoid decision overload.
🚇 Transit is straightforward via Ginza and JR lines.
✂️ First cut if tired: choose either Yanaka or Kappabashi Kitchen Town, not both.

brief.ops: Ginza Line to Asakusa; JR Sobu Line to Akihabara

goal: Old Tokyo in the morning, Cyber Tokyo in the afternoon.

timeline.activity: Optional Yanaka (Pre-War Tokyo Walk). Route: Yanaka Ginza -> temple lanes near Nippori. Skip this if you want more time for Asakusa/Kappabashi.
Senso-ji Temple (Asakusa). Do: Cleanse hands at the fountain. Draw an "Omikuji" (fortune).
Akihabara (Electric Town). Target: Super Potato (Retro Games), Mandarake Complex. Arcade: Taito Station (Gachapon & Ufo catchers).
Kanda Myojin Shrine (Anime shrine).

rainyDayOption: **Akihabara** is surprisingly rain-friendly (big buildings). **Asakusa** has a covered arcade (Nakamise-dori), but the temple grounds are exposed.
keyPhrases: "Menzei dekimazu ka?" (Can I do tax-free?)
"Sumimasen, kore wa doko desu ka?" (Excuse me, where is this? _Show picture of game_)

title: 🚄 Bullet Train to Kyoto
morning: Check out Tokyo base, get to Tokyo Station early, secure ekiben and drinks, then board Nozomi with right-side seating preference for views.
daytime: Arrive Kyoto, drop bags at Cross Hotel, and ease into the city with Nishiki Market sampling instead of a rigid attraction sprint.
night: Use golden hour in Gion, respect no-photo private lanes, and finish with a stroll through Pontocho Alley.
details: 🚄 Major transfer day — protect buffer time around station logistics.
🏨 Hotel shift: Keio Plaza Hotel Shinjuku → Cross Hotel Kyoto Kawaramachi.
note: First intercity rail day. Keep schedule disciplined but calm.

brief.backup: Kyoto Station area shopping if tired
brief.ops: JR Shinjuku→Tokyo Stn (25 min, ¥220); ekiben at Gransta before gates; Nozomi ~10 AM; Mt Fuji ~40 min in on Seat E/right side

goal: Bullet train, Gion, and Pontocho Alley.

timeline.activity: Depart Keio Plaza Hotel → Tokyo Station. Best option: JR from Shinjuku Station (5-min walk from hotel): Chuo Rapid Line direct to Tokyo Station (~25 min, ¥220). Taxi alt: ~¥3,000–4,000, 20–30 min (traffic-dependent).
Arrive Tokyo Station — Shinkansen gates. Ekiben: Buy bento at Gransta food hall BEFORE passing through the Tokaido Shinkansen gates (great selection; closes once through).
Shinkansen (Nozomi). Verify actual car/seat in SmartEX; Seat E side is preferred for Mt Fuji views heading to Kyoto (~40 min into the ride).
Arrive Kyoto Station.
Taxi to Cross Hotel Kyoto. Address Card: Show Japanese Address.
Explore Nishiki Market (400 year old market). Eat: Soy milk donuts, Octopus on a stick.
Gion District (Geisha Spotting). Note: Stay on main streets. Private alleys are "No Photo" zones ($100 fine).

keyPhrases: "Migi-gawa no seki onegaishimasu." (Right side seat please - if needed at ticket counter)
"Kyoto made dono gurai kakarimasu ka?" (How long does it take to Kyoto?)
"Ekiben hitotsu kudasai." (One ekiben / station bento please.)

title: 🦌 Nara Day Trip & Kiyomizu
morning: Make Nara the top priority: use Kyoto Station as the launch point, take Kintetsu to Nara, then focus on Nara Park and Todai-ji before crowds build.
daytime: Keep the Nara loop compact with deer, the Great Buddha, Nakatanidou mochi, and lunch before returning to Kyoto mid-afternoon.
night: Take the Kyoto evening slowly: Kiyomizu-dera, Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka, and golden-hour Gion.
details: 🦌 Nara is the priority today; Arashiyama and Kinkaku-ji are intentionally dropped to keep the route sane.
🚇 Kintetsu Kyoto Line is preferred because Kintetsu Nara Station is closer to Nara Park than JR Nara.
🍘 Buy deer crackers only when ready to feed immediately; keep moving and show open empty hands when out.
☔ Rain backup: Sanjusangendo or Kyoto National Museum.
✂️ First cut if tired: keep Nara, but skip or shorten the Kiyomizu uphill block.
note: Nara-first cultural day with room to linger through Kyoto's evening lanes.

brief.ops: Kintetsu Kyoto→Nara walk-up; IC card OK; Kiyomizu optional if tired

goal: Nara Park, Todai-ji, bowing deer, and a Kyoto evening walk.

timeline.activity: Depart Cross Hotel Kyoto for Kyoto Station, then take the Kintetsu Kyoto Line to Kintetsu Nara Station. Pay with IC card on-site; no advance booking needed.
Nara Park and Todai-ji. Top priority: bowing deer, the Great Buddha, and a relaxed park walk. Buy deer crackers only when ready to feed immediately.
Nakatanidou mochi-pounding shop and lunch near Kintetsu Nara before heading back to Kyoto.
Return Kintetsu Nara → Kyoto Station, then taxi or transit back toward Higashiyama for the evening Kyoto block. If tired, skip Kiyomizu and go straight to Gion/Pontocho Alley.
Kiyomizu-dera (The Wooden Stage). Prepare: uphill walk and stairs, so pace it slowly. Wear sneakers.
Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka slow walk. Browse old-street shops, sweets, ceramics, and photo spots without treating this as a hard stop.
Golden-hour Gion walk. Stay on main streets and respect no-photo private lanes.

rainyDayOption: **Sanjusangen-do** (1001 Kannon Statues) is entirely indoors. **Kyoto National Museum** is across the street.
keyPhrases: "Kintetsu Nara made onegaishimasu." (To Kintetsu Nara, please.)
"Shika senbei wa doko de kaemasu ka?" (Where can I buy deer crackers?)
"Koko wa shashin OK desu ka?" (Is photography OK here?)

title: 🦊 Fushimi Inari & Osaka
morning: Hit Fushimi Inari at early gates and push beyond the first viewpoint for quieter torii sections and better photo rhythm.
daytime: Complete Kyoto checkout, transfer to Osaka, check in near Dotonbori, and leave room for a soft landing before evening crowds.
night: Lean into Osaka's neon core: takoyaki, Glico sign photos, and Hozenji Yokocho for an older-lane contrast to the main strip.
details: 🏨 Hotel shift: Cross Hotel Kyoto Kawaramachi → Cross Hotel Osaka Dotonbori.
🚇 Transfer: Hankyu Kyoto Line from Kyoto-Kawaramachi → Osaka-Umeda (~43 min, ¥430), then Metro to Namba (~5 min, ¥180). Total ~50 min, ~¥610.
🧳 Luggage forwarding: request takkyubin at the hotel front desk the night before (~¥1,000–1,500/bag). Bags arrive at Cross Hotel Osaka by afternoon.
⛩️ Treat Fushimi Inari as the morning highlight; shorten to lower torii loop if Day 6 ran long.
note: Second city move with a high-energy Osaka arrival.

brief.ops: Hankyu from Kyoto-Kawaramachi→Umeda (43 min, ¥430) + Metro to Namba (5 min, ¥180); takkyubin night before recommended; Cross Hotel Osaka check-in 3 PM

goal: Fushimi Inari (The Red Gates) and Neon Dotonbori.

timeline.activity: Fushimi Inari Taisha. Early start beats crowds. If everyone feels good, go past the first lookout (Yotsutsuji); if Day 6 ran long, keep this to the lower torii loop.
Coffee reset and return toward Cross Hotel Kyoto. Confirm bags are packed and ready for checkout.
Check out of Cross Hotel Kyoto.
Transfer to Osaka: Kyoto-Kawaramachi Station → Hankyu Kyoto Line → Osaka-Umeda (~43 min, ¥430) → Metro to Namba (~5 min, ¥180). Total: ~50 min, ~¥610.
Check in Cross Hotel Osaka (Dotonbori). If arriving early, leave bags at the front desk and start the Dotonbori loop hands-free.
Dotonbori Street Food. Eat: Takoyaki (Octopus Balls) at Acchichi Honpo (by the bridge).
Glico Man Sign (Photo Op).
Hozenji Yokocho (Moss Temple alley). Drink: Old-school Izakaya.

keyPhrases: "Takoyaki, hachi-ko kudasai." (8 pieces of Takoyaki please.)
"O-susume wa nan desu ka?" (What do you recommend?)
"Nimotsu wo okutte moraemasuka?" (Can you arrange luggage forwarding? — ask hotel front desk)
"Hankyu Kyoto-sen wa doko desu ka?" (Where is the Hankyu Kyoto Line?)

title: 🏯 Osaka Free Day
splitNote: Split block: Den Den Town vs Shinsaibashi — plan beforehand
morning: Ease into the day with coffee, then explore Osaka Castle grounds for open-space walking and skyline framing shots.
daytime: Use Kuromon Market as the central fuel stop, then split intentionally: Den Den Town (retro/gaming) versus Shinsaibashi (shopping/beauty/sweets).
night: Regroup around Namba/Hozenji and walk Dotonbori at night for photos and snacks.
details: 🧭 Purpose-built flexible day with optional pacing changes.
☔ Easy to adapt for weather because many stops cluster by transit hubs.
🎁 Good day for souvenir and specialty store catches.
📍 Keep meeting checkpoints explicit when splitting up.
🏯 Osaka Castle lives on this day; Day 9 should stay low-risk before the train.
🔀 Optional south-Osaka branch (Shinsekai/Abeno Harukas) only if everyone wants to trade away split-shopping time.
note: Free-form Osaka day designed around both interests.
goal: Flexible Osaka day with a shared morning, split afternoon, and shared dinner.

timeline.activity: Wake up. Coffee and easy start near the hotel.
Head to Osaka Castle for the grounds, photos, and a relaxed morning walk.
Move to Kuromon Market for brunch / snacks.
Split afternoon: Dave to Den Den Town for retro games and arcades; Debbie to Shinsaibashi for shopping, cosmetics, and sweets.
Regroup near Hozenji Yokocho / Namba.
Walk Dotonbori for neon, canal photos, and street snacks.

keyPhrases: "Koko de shashin o totte moraemasu ka?" (Could you take a photo for us here?)
"Osusume wa nan desu ka?" (What do you recommend?)
"Kore wa o-mochikaeri dekimasu ka?" (Can this be taken to go?)

title: 🗼 Return to Tokyo
morning: Keep the final Osaka morning low-risk: breakfast, last Namba/Dotonbori food or souvenirs, then consolidate luggage and move toward Shin-Osaka without rushing.
daytime: Board Shinkansen back to Tokyo area, prioritize easy transfer to Shinagawa/Haneda-side hotel for departure-day confidence.
night: Final Japan dinner near hotel or Haneda Garden, with optional onsen stop if energy remains.
details: 🚄 Last major train move — protect buffer around station transfers.
🚇 Cross Hotel Osaka → Shin-Osaka: walk ~5 min to Namba Station, take Osaka Metro Midosuji Line to Shin-Osaka (~12 min, ¥290). Allow 25 min total.
🎫 Reservation #2005 is already booked for Nozomi at 2:15 PM from Shin-Osaka. Journey to Shinagawa ~2h22m.
🗻 Mt Fuji visible on the left (A seat side) approximately 40 min after Shin-Osaka departure.
🏨 Shinagawa Prince Hotel: 3-min walk from Shinagawa Station Central Exit (west gates), easy to spot.
note: Return logistics day with comfort-first decisions.

brief.ops: Namba→Shin-Osaka: Metro Midosuji (12 min, ¥290); Nozomi Res #2005 at 14:15; Shinagawa Prince 3-min walk from station

goal: Last Osaka bites, Shinkansen to Shinagawa, and final hotel buffer.

timeline.activity: Slow final Osaka morning near Namba/Dotonbori: breakfast, last snacks, pharmacy/convenience-store run, or a Kuromon repeat if desired. Keep this low-risk because the train is fixed.

Head to Shin-Osaka Station. Route: Walk ~5 min to Namba Station → Osaka Metro Midosuji Line → Shin-Osaka Station (~12 min, ¥290). Allow 25 min total including walking and platform time. At Shin-Osaka: Follow 'Shinkansen' signs to the gates. Reservation #2005 is pre-booked.
Board Nozomi (Green Car, Res #2005) to Shinagawa. Duration: ~2 hrs 22 min. Mt Fuji: Visible on the left (A seat side) ~40 min after departure.
Arrive Shinagawa Station.
Check in: Shinagawa Prince Hotel (walk from station). Location: Main Tower, across from Shinagawa Station gates.

keyPhrases: "Kuu-kou wa dochira desu ka?" (Which way is the airport?)
"Saigo no ban-gohan." (Last dinner.)
"Shin-Osaka eki wa doko desu ka?" (Where is Shin-Osaka Station?)

title: 👋 Departure
morning: Slow final morning with breakfast and a controlled last-minute shopping pass (snacks, gifts, duty-free targets).
daytime: Complete checkout, leave Shinagawa by a hard airport-transfer time, and arrive at Haneda with enough margin for check-in, security, and stress-free gate pacing.
night: Board UA130 and begin return to EWR; keep comfort and hydration prioritized for landing recovery.
details: 🛫 Terminal: Haneda T3 (United check-in area typically K/L rows).
⏰ Target airport arrival: around 2:30 PM for a 5:45 PM departure.
🚨 Hard move: leave Shinagawa by about 1:15 PM even if shopping is still tempting.
🎁 Good final buys: Tokyo Banana, Royce, travel-safe sweets.
✅ Closeout task: confirm documents and carry-on essentials before security.
note: Departure day with intentional buffer and low complexity.

brief.ops: Leave Shinagawa by 1:15 PM; keep carry-on essentials ready

goal: Buy last-minute Duty Free. Go home.

timeline.activity: Hard deadline: leave Shinagawa / be en route to Haneda. Do not let shopping eat into the airport buffer.
Check-In UA 130. Counter: Terminal 3, Row K/L usually.
Security & Duty Free. Buy: Famous Tokyo Banana or Royce Chocolate (Need thermal bag).
Flight UA 130 Departs. Seat: Premium Economy. Duration: ~13 Hours.

keyPhrases: "Arigato gozaimashita." (Thank you very much - for the whole trip.)
"Sayonara!" (Goodbye!)
